paper_sections.title: Individual Differences in Anticipatory Somatosensory Cortex Activity for Shock is Positively Related with Trait Anxiety and Multisensory Integration
2.6. General Region of Interest Analysis and Correlation
3.3. Primary Somatosensory Cortex and Individual Differences Analyses

description.value: The study examined fear-conditioning-related somatosensory activity and its relationships with trait anxiety, auditory and amygdala activity, and whole-brain functional connectivity.

design.value: Twenty healthy participants completed an fMRI fear-conditioning task in which low- and high-pitched tones served as conditioned stimuli, one tone was paired with mild electric shock, and CS+ and CS− trials were compared using ROI, correlation, mediation, functional connectivity, and whole-brain analyses.

description.value: An established measure of individual differences in anxiety, providing state anxiety (STAI-S) and trait anxiety (STAI-T) scores.

assessment_type.value: measure of individual differences in anxiety

description.value: Fear contingent responding was assessed using skin conductance response; peak SCR amplitude from baseline was taken between 1–8 s on a trial-by-trial basis then averaged as a function of CS tone.
Participants indicated by button press with their index or middle finger of the right hand whether the tone was low or high pitched immediately after hearing the tone.

source_definition.value: The primary GLM used regressors for non-reinforced CS+ trials and CS− trials.
Trait anxiety score from the Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory.
Six motion parameters were modeled as covariates of no interest.
Shock-reinforced trials were modeled as covariates of no interest in GLM-1.

description.value: Twenty healthy participants (11 female) with mean age of 21.95 (range 18–35) participated in the study.

excluded_count.value: no participants were excluded from the analysis post hoc

inclusion_criteria.value: safe for participation in the MRI environment

exclusion_criteria.value: participants who self-reported having a clinically diagnosed mental illness
participants who reported being on, or having taken in the past, any pharmacological intervention for a mental illness

medical_condition.value: healthy; no clinically diagnosed mental illness

medication_status.value: No participants reported being on, or having taken in the past, any pharmacological intervention for a mental illness.

task_description.value: A total of 30 trials were presented in a random order: 10 CS+ with shock, 10 CS+ without shock and 10 CS− tones. CS+ tones were followed by a shock with a 50% partial reinforcement schedule.

design_type.value: one run; trials presented in a random order

instructions.value: Participants were asked to indicate by button press with their index or middle finger of the right hand whether the tone was low or high pitched immediately after hearing the tone.

stimuli.value: Two tones (500 and 1500 Hz) were adopted as conditioned stimuli; a mild electric shock was delivered to the third and fourth fingers of the left hand as the unconditioned stimulus.

modality.value: functional images with gradient-echo echo-planar T2*-weighted imaging

description.value: Each functional volume consisted of 40 interleaved (no skip) 2.5 mm axial T2*-weighted slices.

acquisition_voxel_size_mm.value: 2.5 mm axial slices; in-plane dimensions not reported

description.value: High-resolution structural images were acquired first.

instrument.value: MP-150 system (BIOPAC System), connected to a grounded RF filter, and MR-compatible leads and electrodes

description.value: Individual skin conductance responses were acquired with MRI-compatible electrodes placed on the index and middle finger of the left hand. All physiological data were recorded at 1 kHz sampling rates.
Standard preprocessing was conducted using FMRIBs Software Library (FSL).

steps.value: spatial smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of full width at half maximum (FWHM) 6 mm
high-pass temporal filtering with a filter width of 100 s
skull stripping of structural images with FSL’s Brain Extraction Tool (BET)
registering each functional image to the participant’s high-resolution structural image and the standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) 2 mm brain
MELODIC ICA2 was applied to remove noise components
The first eight volumes were discarded to allow for signal equilibration.

model_settings.value: Regressors were non-reinforced CS+ trials and CS− trials; six motion parameters and shock-reinforced trials were modeled as covariates of no interest.
The shock epoch on reinforced CS+ trials (500 ms) was modeled, using the same temporal epoch for both non-reinforced CS+ and CS− trials.

Unique trial-by-trial regressors were created for CS+ no shock and CS− trials; global mean signal, motion parameters, and shock trials were included as covariates. Correlation magnitudes were converted into z scores using Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.
The analysis evaluated total effect c, indirect path a, indirect path b, direct effect c’, and mediation effect ab.

description.value: The tone assigned to the CS+ condition was followed by a shock; 10 trials were presented.
CS+ tones were presented without shock; 10 trials were presented.
The CS− tone was presented without shock; 10 trials were presented.

specific_metric.value: Correlation magnitudes converted into z scores using the Fisher’s r-to-z transformation

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) 2 mm brain

parameter_change.value: greater positive functional connectivity during non-reinforced CS+ trials than CS− trials

model_representation_notes.value: Unique trial-by-trial regressors were created for each condition of interest, resulting in 20 independent variables; the global mean signal level over all brain voxels was included to reduce confounding effects of global signal change.

interpretations.value: Right S1 had greater positive functional connectivity with prefrontal regions including the dlPFC and dmPFC during non-reinforced CS+ trials compared to CS− trials.

specific_metric.value: Correlation magnitudes converted into z scores using the Fisher’s r-to-z transformation

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) 2 mm brain

parameter_change.value: lower connectivity during non-reinforced CS+ trials than CS− trials

model_representation_notes.value: Unique trial-by-trial regressors were created for each condition of interest, resulting in 20 independent variables; the global mean signal level over all brain voxels was included to reduce confounding effects of global signal change.

interpretations.value: Right S1 had negative functional connectivity with early visual sensory regions during non-reinforced CS+ trials compared to CS− trials.

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) 2 mm brain

model_representation_notes.value: A gamma-variate function plus temporal derivative was used; six motion parameters and shock-reinforced trials were modeled as covariates of no interest.

interpretations.value: Greater activity for CS+ compared to CS− trials was observed in the putative fear network, including insula, dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, and thalamus, as well as auditory cortices and a larger cluster including parts of the right motor and somatosensory cortices.

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) 2 mm brain

model_representation_notes.value: A gamma-variate function plus temporal derivative was used; six motion parameters and shock-reinforced trials were modeled as covariates of no interest.

interpretations.value: Greater activity for CS− compared to CS+ trials was observed in middle frontal, temporal fusiform, inferior temporal, hippocampal, parahippocampal, postcentral, and frontal regions.
